newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota wheat condition declines despite rains.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota wheat condition declines despite rains.

text.p: North Dakota's spring wheat condition declined despite the arrival of beneficial rains during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"Frequent rain and below-normal temperatures dominated the week, improving many crop prospects but also raising disease concerns and slowing haying operations," the service said in its weekly crop progress report.
Forty-one percent of the state's spring wheat crop rated good or excellent, down from 43 at that level last week. Durum was rated 27 percent good to excellent, against 26 last week.
Small grain development remained ahead of last year but slightly behind average. Spring and durum wheat were 69 and 51 percent in the boot and beyond stage, behind average.
Late season crop continued to grow at a pace slightly ahead of last year and average, with the exception of sugarbeets, potatoes and canola.

Soil moisture continued to be replenished to a level comparable with the five-year average. Topsoil moisture conditions were rated 19 percent short to very short, against 44 in that category last week, 19 percent last year and the average of 12 percent.
